purpose: Identify disruptions that maximise post-disruption total system travel time after travellers re-route under user equilibrium.

mathematical_formulation.upper_level: max_{y in Y(B)} sum_a v_a*(y) t_a(v_a*(y),y_a)
mathematical_formulation.lower_level: v*(y) in argmin_v sum_a integral_0^{v_a} t_a(s,y_a) ds
mathematical_formulation.flow_conservation: sum_{p in P_rs} f_p=q_rs; v_a=sum_{rs,p} delta_ap f_p

unlock_rule: Disabled until an OD matrix, capacities and declared volume-delay functions are supplied and an equilibrium solver is configured.

primary_sources.citation: Wardrop (1952), Some theoretical aspects of road traffic research, Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers.
Colson, Marcotte and Savard (2005), Bilevel programming: a survey, 4OR.
Yang and Bell (1998), Models and algorithms for road network design, Transport Reviews.

known_limitations: Bilevel equilibrium models can be nonconvex and expensive.
UE assumptions may not represent evacuation behaviour.
UE convergence gap and upper-level optimality evidence are mandatory.
